title: Bouncing ball

reference.basis: no label, caption or narration states its length so length unknown

slow_motion.evidence: no on-screen text, narration or visual indicator of slow motion; motion plays as continuous real-time animation

subjects.description: small orange circular ball with white highlight that falls and bounces rightward

observation.what_happens: An orange ball drops from the upper left and then travels rightward while bouncing low above the brown floor. The motion starts as it falls from its initial position and ends while it is still moving to the right near the right side of the frame.

calibration.note: scale from the fall itself: 356 px/s² over 4 arcs = g of 9.807 m/s²

given: g = 9.807 m/s² (Earth); it set the scale, so treat g as known and fixed
reasoning: x advances almost steadily while y shows two large parabolic arcs with sharp turnarounds near -7.1 m, classic projectile bounces. Rise heights give e near 0.83. Candidates keep textbook flight plus a bounce event, then add linear and quadratic air drag plus horizontal scuff to test the unseen bounces.

headline: Bouncing ball flies free and keeps its bounce
finding: The ball falls under gravity 9.81 m/s² and hits the floor at -7.68 ± 0.02 m, bouncing back with 0.85 ± 0.0002 dimensionless of its speed.

eyeball.law_in_words: vertical outgoing speed equals e times vertical incoming speed, and at contact the ball centre is one radius above the floor
